name: Ferroxan
description: A vasodilating compound laced with synthetic catecholamines that floods augmented musculature and servomechanical joints with supercharged hydraulic pressure and electrical conductivity, pushing mechanical augments 30-50% beyond their rated output for a brief window. Designed originally as an emergency extraction compound for trapped workers with industrial chrome, it was rapidly weaponized by street operators. The come-down is brutal — joints seize, micro-tears form in the biological tissue anchoring the chrome to bone.
effects: Augmented limb strength increased 30-50% beyond rated spec
Reaction time for chrome-assisted movement reduced by 40ms
Thermal output from chrome increases — augments run hot
side_effects: Anchor-point micro-tears where chrome meets bone
Joint seizure on come-down (1-4 hours of reduced mobility)
Risk of servo burnout in lower-grade augments
Cardiac arrhythmia in users with chest-cavity chrome
Permanent joint degradation with repeated use
cultural_context: Called 'Redline' because users are literally running their chrome past the manufacturer's red-line safety threshold. A staple of Shelf pit-fighters and street enforcers who can't afford better augments and need to compete with people who have higher-grade chrome. Tier 2 mechanics joke that they can identify Ferroxan users by the joint damage on their chrome — looks like someone put a car engine through a drag race every weekend for a year.
story_hooks: A Shelf enforcer has been running Ferroxan so long her anchor points are failing — her arm chrome is literally working loose from her humerus, and she needs one more job to pay for surgical re-anchoring before it detaches completely.

A batch of Ferroxan has been cut with an unknown compound that doesn't just overclock chrome — it seems to be rewriting servo firmware, and users are reporting their augments moving on their own after the high fades.

A Tier 3 augment technician is quietly buying Ferroxan in bulk — not to use, but to study, claiming Nightshade accidentally solved a mechanical efficiency problem that Lazarus has spent decades trying to crack legitimately.
